scientist_stages.title: Provide organism, sequence, annotation, and diffraction inputs
scientist_stages.summary: Supply the biological source, the proteins that may be tested, their genome and annotation context when available, and the measured diffraction data.
scientist_stages.purpose: Keep every biological and diffraction input separate and make sure later steps cannot mix files, organisms, or crystals.
inputs: Scientific species name plus strain/assembly identity — required to resolve the correct genome, annotation, and proteome, but not yet dedicated manifest fields
Diffraction MTZ file and crystal name — required
Run settings and installed reference-database descriptions
outputs: Resolved genome, annotation, and proteome source identities
A checked record of the biological source and protein sequences
Optional genome and annotation context retained when supplied
A checked record of each diffraction file
A record of the exact inputs used by every later step
decisions: Use one annotation source for the protein list
Stop when a required file is missing, changed, duplicated, or malformed
Keep every possible gene location when two entries have the same protein sequence
boundaries: A structure found in an external database cannot add a new protein identity that was absent from the supplied list
Missing genome, annotation files, or molecular-weight evidence remains explicitly optional
Localisation evidence is derived internally from the protein FASTA with PSORTb and DeepTMHMM
The workflow trusts the supplied protein list; it does not predict genes or assign taxonomy
Species-to-genome/proteome source resolution and dedicated species/assembly fields are not yet implemented
A species may have multiple strains or reference assemblies, so exact source resolution requires strain or assembly identity in addition to the species name
scientist_stages.warning: The workflow records file checksums so results cannot silently switch to a changed input file.

scientist_stages.title: Crystallographic preflight
scientist_stages.summary: Select observations, symmetry, resolution, anisotropy, Patterson evidence, and the exact Free-R source before model discovery.
scientist_stages.purpose: Qualify each diffraction dataset before the workflow proceeds to model discovery.
decisions: Continue to model discovery with qualified diffraction data
Retain non-fatal warnings for later review
Fail on a missing usable observation selection or another fatal diffraction-data condition
boundaries: Preflight qualifies data; it does not identify a protein
The scientist overview shows no interactive pause between preflight and model discovery
Phenix is an external licensed runtime and is never installed by the workflow
scientist_stages.warning: Preflight and model discovery are shown sequentially; implementation-level file contracts remain in the developer view.
commands: pixi run -e hpc nextflow run qualification.nf --operation mtz_preflight -stub-run

scientist_stages.title: Find and prepare protein structure models
scientist_stages.summary: For every supplied protein sequence, search local structure databases for related experimental structures or explicitly mapped predictions, then convert valid coordinates into models that Molecular Replacement can test.
scientist_stages.purpose: Produce a checked set of protein structure models while keeping the search result, the prepared coordinate file, and the supplied protein identity distinct.
inputs: Groups of identical sequences from the supplied protein list
Qualified local PDB SEQRES database for MMseqs2
Qualified local PDB100 database plus the ProstT5 model for Foldseek
Installed Gemmi runtime and, for predicted models, the verified Phenix runtime
outputs: MMseqs2 and Foldseek hit, no-hit, and ineligible records
Downloaded or locally registered coordinate sources with checksums
Prepared protein structure models linked to the supplied protein sequence
A complete registry that also records proteins with no eligible model
decisions: MMseqs2/PDB SEQRES: keep hits with E-value at most 1e-5 and at least 50% query coverage
ProstT5/Foldseek/PDB100: keep hits with E-value at most 1e-3 and at least 50% query coverage
Retain at most three normalised hits per protein from each local PDB search route
Use AlphaFold DB only when an explicit accession map connects it to the supplied protein
Keep ESM Atlas disabled unless remote sequence submission is explicitly enabled
Reject missing chains, checksum changes, sequence mismatches, malformed coordinates, and unsupported multi-model inputs
boundaries: A database hit proposes a model; it does not prove which protein is in the crystal
Every reportable identity must come from the supplied protein list
PDB models are cleaned with Gemmi by retaining the mapped polymer chain and removing non-polymer atoms and hydrogens
Exact predicted models are confidence-pruned with phenix.process_predicted_model
Normal analysis runs use prepared, versioned databases and never silently rebuild them
scientist_stages.warning: A completed no-hit means that one search route found no model under its stated criteria; it is not an execution failure and does not prove the protein is absent.

scientist_stages.title: Rank candidates and run the one-copy screen
scientist_stages.summary: Retain the complete configured Matthews expected-copy alternatives, but search exactly one copy in every initial Molecular Replacement task.
scientist_stages.purpose: Narrow the candidate space into reviewable one-copy A seeds while preserving expected-copy alternatives, raw evidence, resources, and deferred reasons.
inputs: Protein identities from the supplied list and their prepared models
Workflow-derived PSORTb and DeepTMHMM localisation evidence
Optional user-provided molecular-weight evidence bound at the beginning of the analysis
outputs: Matthews priors across the configured expected-copy range
Per-hypothesis Phaser commands, placements, scores, and status records
decisions: Preserve every physically possible configured expected-copy alternative
Search exactly one copy in every initial task
Add copies only sequentially after explicit A approval
Apply the 25-hypothesis limit independently to each crystal
Treat rank and Matthews probability as priors
Continue sibling hypotheses after candidate-specific scientific failure
boundaries: SDS-PAGE mass is an apparent monomer prior, never ASU total mass
Expected copy count is a prior, not observed support
A placement is search evidence until reviewed
Rfree is not a high-throughput screening objective
scientist_stages.maturity: local and CI qualified; fixed-HPC acceptance pending
scientist_stages.warning: No joint-copy or four-copy admission ceiling is part of the active initial screen.

scientist_stages.title: Review, refine, and read maps
scientist_stages.summary: Confirm the reviewed first-component structure, refine retained states, inspect maps, and narrow identity only as far as the evidence supports.
scientist_stages.purpose: Turn machine-ranked placements into human-reviewed structural states with explicit claim and abstention boundaries.
inputs: Recorded decision for the first placed component
outputs: Approved, rejected, or deferred seed state
decisions: Resolve decisions only through the registered review package
Accept ambiguity or abstention
Separate malformed output from a scientific no-hit
boundaries: Map support may be insufficient to distinguish paralogues or loci
Rwork/Rfree and map-model fit must remain visible
A review decision cannot invent an unregistered state
scientist_stages.warning: Real Phenix and fixed-HPC qualification remain incomplete for some paths.

scientist_stages.title: Bounded composition expansion
scientist_stages.summary: After reviewing the first component, evaluate candidate gene products from the supplied list as possible heteromer partners. Each hypothesis adds one candidate gene product to the retained component set.
scientist_stages.purpose: Test whether a candidate gene product can work with the retained component or components as a heteromer, without selecting one partner in advance or treating search exhaustion as proof that the composition is complete.
inputs: Reviewed first-component structure or another approved retained state
Candidate gene products and their eligible structure models
Parent-bound expansion plan and reviewer composition decisions
outputs: Per-depth attempt inventories and retained parent states
Claim-free terminal composition and sequence review packages
decisions: Retain at most three parent states before each expansion depth
Exclude gene products already represented in the retained state
Create competing hypotheses that each add one candidate gene product
Retain configured physically possible copy alternatives without a separate four-copy ceiling
Rank hypotheses by localisation, molecular-weight evidence, total-composition Matthews plausibility, model quality, and structural diversity
Bound work to 25 attempts per depth and 100 partner attempts per crystal
Stop on depth, budget, no-model, review hold, or no residual content
boundaries: The workflow does not manually choose one partner before testing
One hypothesis adds one candidate gene product to its retained parent state
Depth three is positively qualified by 9ECN
Depths four through six are always provisional
No automatic identity or complete-composition claim is made between depths
scientist_stages.warning: Depths 4-6 remain visible but unvalidated and cannot support a complete-composition claim.

scientist_stages.title: Reviewed report and evidence package
scientist_stages.summary: Assemble checksummed results that distinguish supported findings, ambiguity, no-hit, provisional depth, held status, and execution failure.
scientist_stages.purpose: Publish a portable, auditable conclusion whose strength never exceeds the reviewed evidence.
inputs: All owned stage outputs and raw metrics
Execution, environment, database, and checksum manifests
decisions: Refuse claims when required review or source records are absent
Keep scientific status separate from execution status
Publish no-hit and ambiguity as valid completed analyses
boundaries: Models remain hypotheses unless supported by diffraction and review
Exact locus identity is withheld when the map cannot discriminate it
Deeper private analysis remains blocked until every required review gate is complete
scientist_stages.maturity: implemented; deeper private analysis not authorised
scientist_stages.warning: Visible implementation is not run authorisation: required review evidence is still incomplete.

developer_layers.title: Reviewed control plane
developer_layers.summary: Stages only clean immutable commits, fixed profiles, owned inputs, and reviewed site bindings.
developer_layers.purpose: Keep deployment, scheduler submission, collection, and source-of-truth checks outside scientific services and under reviewed run control.
inputs: Owned run inputs and capability records
decisions: Reject dirty or unreachable source
Permit only reviewed profile/site pairs
Collect and classify before changing code
boundaries: The local repository is the only source of truth
HPC source is never edited
Permission to submit does not imply scientific acceptance
developer_layers.warning: Qualification evidence is exact-source and site-specific.

developer_layers.title: Application entrypoints
developer_layers.summary: phase3_application.nf is the current transitional Phase III entrypoint. The large clean break converges the public application into main.nf beside prepare_databases.nf.
developer_layers.purpose: Expose one explicit application entrypoint and keep database preparation separate from normal analysis.
outputs: Final public main.nf after clean break
decisions: Reject parameters belonging to another entrypoint
Keep prepare_databases.nf separate
Remove superseded roots without compatibility shims
boundaries: Archival main.nf remains v0.2 during transition
phase3_application.nf is not the final public name
Validation remains outside normal analysis
developer_layers.warning: The final main.nf clean break has not yet occurred.

developer_layers.title: Typed Nextflow workflows
developer_layers.summary: DSL2 workflows own channel-item fan-out, scheduling, retries, resume, and publication.
developer_layers.purpose: Express dependency and concurrency without hiding scientific loops inside scripts.
decisions: Fan out independent work
Keep dependent chains explicit
Let the configured executor own concurrency
boundaries: Nextflow does not decide scientific rank or claims
Attempt budgets remain scientific contracts
Cache identity changes with scientific semantics
developer_layers.warning: Individual workflow paths retain separate HPC qualification status.

developer_layers.title: Thin process modules
developer_layers.summary: Each adapter binds typed inputs and performs one efficiently bounded external or Python task.
developer_layers.purpose: Make every scheduled task auditable, cacheable, and independently testable.
decisions: Use efficient batch boundaries
Fail malformed outputs close to the adapter
Keep shell wrappers limited to environment binding
boundaries: No nested scheduler or hidden multi-sample loop
Candidate no-hit is not process failure
Licensed runtimes remain external
developer_layers.warning: Real-runtime qualification varies by external adapter.

developer_layers.title: Python scientific services and contracts
developer_layers.summary: Small services own validation, policy, planning, parsing, status derivation, identifiers, and schemas.
developer_layers.purpose: Centralise scientific invariants and typed state transitions without taking over workflow scheduling.
decisions: Reject malformed or unknown state
Preserve raw metrics
Keep identity, model, and evidence universes separate
boundaries: Python does not schedule independent tasks
Ranks and priors do not become proof
Historical readers stay isolated from active contracts
developer_layers.warning: Active milestone-named surfaces remain queued for the clean break.

developer_layers.title: External runtime boundaries
developer_layers.summary: Phenix, MMseqs2, Foldseek, PSORTb, DeepTMHMM, Slurm, and containers remain narrow versioned adapters.
developer_layers.purpose: Record external commands, versions, licensing, network, and failure behaviour without importing external internals into the application.
inputs: Explicit permission for network or licensed runtime use
decisions: Require explicit remote-sequence consent
Verify Phenix instead of installing it
Keep compute-node network assumptions explicit
boundaries: No automatic Phenix download
Normal analyses never build databases
Provider no-hit remains distinct from outage
developer_layers.warning: Consult the boundary page for each tool's exact qualification state.

developer_layers.title: Evidence, review, and publication
developer_layers.summary: Owned packages, immutable manifests, file-based review, cache records, and verified reports carry every result forward.
developer_layers.purpose: Make every decision and published conclusion traceable to exact source, inputs, commands, and evidence bytes.
decisions: Resolve only registered review packages
Publish no-hit and ambiguity honestly
Refuse claims above validated scope
boundaries: Review is file-based, never interactive on compute nodes
Collection does not upgrade maturity
Private inputs stay outside tracked documentation
developer_layers.warning: All required review evidence must be complete before deeper private analysis.
